summary: Master crisis management with Design Thinking! Learn to craft innovative, human-centered emergency response strategies that protect businesses and people.
lede: Design Thinking for Crisis Management and Emergency Response helps you identify response friction, understand affected people and stakeholders, and shape workable interventions under pressure. You will connect user needs with incident command discipline while addressing unclear priorities, fragmented communication, delayed escalation, and competing operational demands. The course guides you through practical tools including stakeholder mapping, journey mapping, impact and urgency prioritization, escalation matrices, decision logs, scenario testing, and after-action reviews. You will also explore risk-informed response concepts, business impact analysis, information-flow design, PACE communication planning, and dashboard logic using Power BI or Excel, with practical introductions to ISO 31000, ISO 22301, ISO 22320, the Design Council Double Diamond, the Incident Command System, and the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who already contribute to crisis management, emergency response, continuity, resilience, or operational risk and need to improve how response solutions work in practice. It suits experienced practitioners who want a structured human-centered method for examining response gaps, designing interventions, and communicating decisions to leadership.
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to emergency planning, business continuity, operational risk, crisis communications, safety, security, or resilience activities. Familiarity with incident plans, tabletop exercises, or business impact analysis will help, but you do not need prior Design Thinking certification or advanced analytics experience. No coding or programming is required. AI-assisted response design and dashboard work receive operational application treatment, while full enterprise deployment and technical engineering remain outside the course scope. Bring a current, anonymized response challenge if available.
